subject: Preparing a room for installation
hook: The first thing our fitters pick up isn't a drill. It's a level.
ig:
The first thing our fitters pick up isn't a drill. It's a level.

Before a single panel goes up, the team checks what the room is actually doing. Floors slope, walls bow, and corners are rarely a true right angle, especially in older houses.

Here's what happens in that first half hour:

- The floor is checked so base units can be packed up level from the start.
- The wall is measured against the survey drawings.
- Any bows or dips are marked so filler panels can be scribed to fit.
- The route in is checked so panels can come through without knocks.

This is why a clear, finished room matters. If the wall is still being plastered or the hallway is full of boxes, those checks take longer and the fit slows down.

It's all part of the same job: furniture made in our Hanley workshop and fitted by our own team.

Comment FIT and we'll send you our installation page, or tap the link in bio.
fb:
Ever wondered what fitters actually do when they first arrive?

In our case, it's checking the room before anything gets fixed. Floor levels, wall bows, the route in from the van. Older houses around Staffordshire are full of character, which usually means nothing is quite straight. Finding that out at the start is what lets the finished furniture look like it grew there.

This short clip shows how our own team starts a fit. It's also why we ask for a clear, finished room on the day.
